_description: Material library recipe extracted from /Game/VFX/EnergyBeam/_GenericSource/Material. Use this when the agent needs to learn how a reusable VFX material library is structured for sprites, beams, ribbons, plasma, cylindrical volumes, decals, and distortion.
overview: This library is not one hero material. It is a modular generic-source pack. The dominant logic is: keep base sprite materials simple, build beam/ribbon materials around directional flow, build cylindrical/twist materials around local-space volume deformation, and keep decals/distortion as separate utility families rather than mixing all logic into one graph.
library_design_rules: Use a small set of reusable base materials and create variants for additive, anti-aliased, panning, flipbook, ribbon, cylindrical twist, decal, and distortion use cases.
Do not put sprite, ribbon, volume shell, and decal logic into one giant benchmark graph.
Let Niagara drive timing, per-particle color, and motion. Let the material handle shape, flow, edge treatment, and view-dependent polish.
Prefer unlit translucent or additive for most energy reads; only use default-lit or opaque when the material is intentionally surface-bound or PBR-integrated.
Treat this folder as a source library to pick from, adapt, or instance, not as a single effect recipe.

sprite_base.purpose: Generic sprite particles for sparks, embers, motes, glows, and soft accents.
dominant_logic: ParticleColor-driven tinting
simple mask texture or radial math shape
optional UV utility and alpha-channel switching
optional depth fade or lightweight edge shaping
SubUV or flipbook support when animated sprite sheets are needed
selection_rules: Use M_Vfx_Basic as the default translucent sprite base.
Use M_Vfx_BasicAdd when you want hotter additive bloom and can tolerate reduced shape retention.
Use M_Vfx_Basic_AA when edge cleanliness matters more than raw intensity.
Use M_Vfx_Basic_Pan when a sprite needs scrolling internal energy instead of a static blob.
Use M_Vfx_ParticleSubUV or M_Vfx_FlipBook when motion is stored in a sheet rather than Niagara shape logic.
Use M_Vfx_MathCircleDot or M_Vfx_Color when you need an ultra-cheap procedural dot/glow.

beam_and_ribbon.purpose: Directional beam bodies, streaks, arc lines, and ribbon-based energy rays.
dominant_logic: directional panning along beam or ribbon length
contained emissive core with controlled opacity
edge support or HDR shaping for hot streak readability
radial gradient support for beam centers or launch glows
selection_rules: Use M_Vfx_RibbonRay for the simpler ribbon streak case.
Use M_Vfx_RibbonBeamRay when the beam needs more hierarchy than a plain ribbon streak.
Use M_Vfx_BeamLightning only for very minimal lightning reads or prototyping; it is too simple for hero beams by itself.
Use M_Vfx_Launch and M_Vfx_PowerEssence as support materials for charge/release moments, not as full beam-body replacements.
Use M_Vfx_HdrEdge when a beam or pulse needs hotter edge energy and richer internal flow.

volume_and_twist.purpose: Local-space cylindrical or plasma volume reads for vortexes, rotating cores, energy columns, and twisting shell-like volumes.
dominant_logic: local-space or volume-oriented mapping
cylindrical twist or internal spin
WorldPositionOffset support for silhouette motion
opacity and emissive working together to suggest a contained moving volume
selection_rules: Use M_Vfx_Plasma for a relatively light plasma-shell or plasma-core read.
Use M_Vfx_CylTwistCore when the effect needs a readable inner energetic column rather than a flat sprite.
Use M_Vfx_CylTwist when silhouette masking and lit/surface interaction matter more than a pure emissive core.
Use the water variants only when the read should stay fluid rather than electrical or arcane.

decal_family.purpose: Surface-bound marks, spell circles, and impact/decal overlays.
dominant_logic: projection or surface-bound alignment
decal layering separated from particle materials
optionally lit/PBR-aware response for grounded marks
selection_rules: Use M_Vfx_DecalSpellAdd when emissive additive projection is the main read.
Use M_Vfx_DecalMark when a lit translucent mark should sit on geometry with stronger surface integration.
Use M_Vfx_DecalMark_PBR when the decal must respect more grounded PBR context.

distortion_utility.purpose: Heat/energy refraction and normal-driven screen-space breakup.
dominant_logic: panning normal-based distortion
very light opacity support
utility role rather than primary emissive look
selection_rules: Keep distortion as a separate support layer.
Do not ask distortion to also carry the hero color or shape read.

surface_lit_utility.purpose: Very simple wall or surface utility materials that sit closer to environment/surface reads than VFX particle reads.
dominant_logic: simple lit surface color/emissive support
not intended as a particle default
selection_rules: Do not pick this as the default for sparks, embers, or beams.

logic: single mask texture or radial shape
Opacity and EmissiveColor as primary pins
optional alpha interpretation or edge shaping
flipbook or subUV texture sheet lookup
Niagara-driven frame animation / renderer subUV support
panning along beam or ribbon UV
opacity shaping to avoid full-screen flood
hue or HDR manipulation for stronger energy accents
surface grounding or emissive overlay depending on variant

if_the_effect_needs.need: generic ember, spark, or magic mote

authoring_guidance_for_forgepilot: When a prompt matches sparks, embers, or small magic particles, start from the sprite_base family before authoring a new graph from scratch.
When a prompt matches beams, rays, or ribbon energy, prefer the beam_and_ribbon family over adapting a sprite material.
When a prompt needs twisting local-space volume, prefer the volume_and_twist family instead of forcing the look through layered sprites alone.
Keep distortion separate from the hero color/shading material.
If the target effect mixes multiple families, split them into separate material assignments per emitter or renderer role.
common_failure_modes: trying to use a base sprite material for a beam body that really needs directional flow
trying to use a ribbon or cylindrical twist material for generic sparks or embers
putting distortion into the main hero material instead of a support layer
treating this generic-source folder as one single benchmark graph instead of a modular toolkit
collapsing sprite, beam, volume, and decal semantics into one catch-all material

agent_recipe.step_1: Classify the requested look into one primary family: sprite_base, beam_and_ribbon, volume_and_twist, decal_family, distortion_utility, or surface_lit_utility.
agent_recipe.step_2: Choose the closest source material from the family before proposing graph edits.
agent_recipe.step_3: Only add complexity that matches the family logic already present in the library.
agent_recipe.step_4: If one effect needs multiple visual roles, assign different materials per emitter/layer instead of forcing one graph to do everything.
agent_recipe.step_5: Expose artist-facing parameters for color, emissive, flow speed, contrast, and edge control, but keep the base graph readable.
